content.title: About
content.content: Fennel is a perennial herb of the Apiaceae family cultivated for its edible bulb. Raw fennel bulb is crisp, mildly sweet with a hint of anise, and is used in salads, pickles, and as a garnish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The bulb is rich in aromatic compounds, especially anethole, which gives it its distinctive scent.
Ancient Romans used fennel as a remedy for digestive complaints.
While fennel seeds are widely known, the bulb remains a regional specialty in Mediterranean cuisine.
Commercial varieties are selected for compact bulbs rather than plant height, which can reach up to 1.5 m.
In some cultures fennel symbolizes purity and appears in festive dishes.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: The bulb provides vitamin C, supporting immune function and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Good source of fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber promotes healthy digestion and contributes to satiety.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and normal blood pressure.

items.title: Antioxidant content
items.content: Flavonoids and phenolic compounds in fennel protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Anethole stimulates bile production, aiding the digestion of fats.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fennel, ranging from skin rash to swelling.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Fennel can enhance the effects of anticoagulants, so caution is advised for people on blood thinners.

items.title: Thyroid considerations
items.content: Large amounts of fennel may affect thyroid function due to its goitrogenic compounds.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw fennel bulb is thinly sliced and added to salads, pickles, or used as a crunchy garnish for fish and meat dishes. It can also be lightly sautéed or roasted to soften the flavor while retaining its aroma.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fennel in the refrigerator, wrapped in a damp towel or placed in a perforated bag. It stays fresh for up to two weeks. Remove wilted leaves and discard any parts that show signs of rot.
